groups.title: Basics
items: One bag per person, with supplies for at least 1 to 3 days.
Use a backpack you can carry. Keep the weight to about 15 kg for men and 10 kg for women at most.
Keep it near the front door. You can keep a lighter bag by the bed, in the car, or at work.
Check it every six months. Eat food that is about to expire and replace it.

groups.title: Checklist
groups.note: tick items off; your ticks stay on this phone only
items: Drinking water: the Ministry of National Defense suggests two 600 ml bottles; the National Fire Agency suggests 15 ml per kg of body weight per day.
Food that needs no cooking: canned food, instant rice, ration biscuits, energy bars, nuts, chocolate. Choose items that keep at room temperature and don't make you thirsty.
Hygiene: masks, tissues, wet wipes, rubbing alcohol, sanitary products, a small towel, a portable water filter.
Medical: regular and prescription medicine, wound ointment, bandages, a thermometer, spare glasses.
Light: a flashlight or headlamp with spare batteries.
Communication: a whistle, a portable radio, and a paper list of contacts (family meeting point, phone numbers, government hotlines).
Warmth and sun: a raincoat, a jacket, a blanket or emergency foil blanket, a hat, sunscreen.

Documents: copies of your ID, health insurance card, and bankbook in a waterproof bag; if you are a foreign resident, also copies of your passport and ARC (added by this app); some cash, including coins.
Power: a charged power bank, charging cables, batteries.
Tools: cut-resistant gloves, plastic bags, a helmet, paper and pen, a lighter, a multi-tool, a can opener, comfortable walking shoes.

groups.title: If your household includes
items: Babies: formula, bottles, baby food, diapers, a baby carrier, a pacifier or small toy.
Older adults: easy-to-eat food such as nutrition jelly, adult diapers, a spare cane, denture care items, hearing aids and batteries, reading glasses.
Pets: pet food, regular medicine, a carrier, a leash, a blanket, owner contact details.

blocks.source: Sources: All-out Defense Mobilization Agency, Ministry of National Defense; National Fire Agency, Ministry of the Interior

sections.title: What to do in a disaster

groups.title: Earthquake
items: Protect your head and neck: Drop, Cover, and Hold On until the shaking stops.
Indoors: take cover under a sturdy table or in a corner. Don't run outside. Hold on to the table legs. Watch out for cabinets, lights, and appliances.
Outdoors: stop walking, stay away from things that could fall, and crouch in an open area. Don't run into buildings.
Driving: slow down, turn on your hazard lights, stop in an open area, and stay in the car until the shaking stops.
If damage is severe: take your go-bag and follow rescue workers to an evacuation shelter.

blocks.source: Sources: National Fire Agency, Ministry of the Interior; All-out Defense Mobilization Agency

groups.title: Typhoon
items: When a typhoon warning is issued, check your home supplies and go-bag, get home early, and stay indoors.
If damage is severe, take your go-bag and evacuate as instructed.

groups.title: Tsunami
items: Be alert after a strong earthquake near the coast, when you receive a tsunami warning message, when you hear the tsunami siren, or when the sea pulls back quickly or white waves approach from far away.
Tsunami siren: 5 seconds on, 5 seconds off, 5 seconds on, followed by a "tsunami warning" announcement. A continuous 90-second tone means the warning is lifted.
Move to high ground away from the coast right away, for example the 3rd floor or higher of a sturdy building. Don't wait for a warning, and don't go to the shore to look.
Don't drive for short-distance evacuation. You could get stuck in traffic or trapped in the car.
If you can't reach high ground in time, hold on to something solid, such as a large tree or steel bars.
More waves may follow the first. Don't go home or near a fishing port or the beach until the warning is lifted.

blocks.source: Sources: Central Weather Administration; All-out Defense Mobilization Agency

groups.title: Debris flow
items: Warning signs: tilting trees or poles, water seeping from slopes, sudden cracks in the ground, loud rumbling from the mountains, or river water suddenly turning muddy with mud and driftwood.
If you see signs or receive a warning, take your go-bag and move to higher ground right away.
Don't run along the path of a stream or debris flow. Stay away from streams, slopes, drains, and bridges.

groups.title: Fire
items: Your life comes first. Don't go back for belongings. Don't use the elevator, and don't hide in the bathroom.
Go down and out. Smoke rises much faster than people can climb, so don't go upstairs.
Before opening a door, touch the top of it. If it's hot, don't open it; use another way out. If it's not hot, open it a little and check for smoke before going out.
Close doors behind you to keep fire and smoke in.
If the stairway is full of smoke, don't go up or through the smoke. Look for another exit.

If both exits are blocked, go to the room or balcony farthest from the fire that has a window to the outside. Close the door, block the gap with clothes, call 119, give your exact location, and wait for rescue.

blocks.source: Source: National Fire Agency, Ministry of the Interior
